#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prometheus scrape targets must name the port each service actually listens on (KS-971).
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. Every target in the `secuura-services` job was wrong, and had been for as long
# as the file has existed: it scraped `secuura-auth:3001` while auth listens on 4003, and the same
# for all seven. The `secuura-gateway` job named `secuura-nginx-gateway:6882` — the HOST side of a
# `6882:80` publish, so a port nothing listens on inside the network.
#
# None of it failed loudly. A Prometheus target that cannot connect goes `down` on a status page
# nobody opens, and the config carried a comment pre-excusing exactly that ("Services that do not
# yet implement /metrics will produce scrape errors ... this is expected and non-blocking"), so the
# one signal that something was wrong had already been explained away in advance.
#
# The compose file is the authority: a service's port is `PORT=<n>` in its environment, and that is
# also what it binds. This suite compares the two and fails when they disagree.
#
# No Docker required — both inputs are files in the repo.

set -uo pipefail

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
DEV_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)"
COMPOSE="${COMPOSE_FILE_UNDER_TEST:-$DEV_ROOT/docker-compose.yml}"
PROM="${PROMETHEUS_YML_UNDER_TEST:-$DEV_ROOT/../../observability/prometheus/prometheus.yml}"

PASS=0
FAIL=0

# `expect` is also /usr/bin/expect. Define ours and refuse to run if the name did not bind to a
# function, or every case would shell out to the binary and pass vacuously.
check() {
    local desc="$1" want="$2" got="$3"
    if [[ "$want" == "$got" ]]; then
        PASS=$((PASS + 1))
        echo "ok   $desc"
    else
        FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
        echo "FAIL $desc"
        echo "       want: $want"
        echo "       got : $got"
    fi
}
expect() { check "$@"; }
if [[ "$(type -t expect)" != "function" ]]; then
    echo "FATAL: expect did not bind to our function" >&2
    exit 2
fi

for f in "$COMPOSE" "$PROM"; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || {
        echo "FATAL: missing input $f" >&2
        exit 2
    }
done

echo "prometheus_targets:"

# --- ground truth: <service> <PORT> from the compose environment -------------
# awk, not mapfile/declare -A — macOS ships bash 3.2 (check-script-portability.sh rule 7).
service_ports=$(
    awk '
        /^  [a-z0-9-]+:$/            { svc = $1; sub(/:$/, "", svc) }
        /container_name:.*STACK_PREFIX/ { name = $0; sub(/.*}-/, "", name); cn[svc] = name }
        /- *PORT=[0-9]+/             { p = $0; sub(/.*PORT=/, "", p); sub(/[^0-9].*/, "", p);
                                       if (svc != "" && cn[svc] != "") print cn[svc], p }
    ' "$COMPOSE" | sort -u
)

# --- what prometheus actually scrapes ----------------------------------------
# Comment lines are stripped first, the way check-script-portability.sh does it: this file and the
# config both DESCRIBE the wrong addresses in prose, and a check that cannot tell a description from
# a declaration would fail on its own documentation.
prom_live=$(sed 's/#.*//' "$PROM")
prom_targets=$(grep -oE "'secuura-[a-z0-9-]+:[0-9]+'" <<<"$prom_live" | tr -d "'" | sed 's/^secuura-//' | sort -u)

# --- NON-VACUITY: both sides must be non-empty -------------------------------
# Without this the comparison below passes trivially the moment either parser stops matching —
# a green tick that means "I found nothing to check".
expect "compose yielded service ports to compare" "yes" \
    "$([[ -n "$service_ports" ]] && echo yes || echo no)"
expect "prometheus.yml yielded scrape targets to compare" "yes" \
    "$([[ -n "$prom_targets" ]] && echo yes || echo no)"

# --- the alerting env example must not suggest the gateway's HOST port (KS-1388) ---
# observability/config/alerting.env.example offers SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI as a commented override. The
# exporter runs on the container network, where only 80 exists (the 6882 host publish is unreachable
# there). observability/docker-compose.yml already defaults to :80; the example must agree with it.
expect "observability/config/alerting.env.example suggests the gateway's in-network status port" \
    "# SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI=http://secuura-nginx-gateway:80/stub_status" \
    "$(grep -m1 'SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI=' "$DEV_ROOT/../../observability/config/alerting.env.example")"

# --- every scraped target must name the port that service listens on ---------
mismatches=""
while IFS= read -r target; do
    [[ -n "$target" ]] || continue
    svc="${target%%:*}"
    port="${target##*:}"
    real=$(awk -v s="$svc" '$1 == s { print $2 }' <<<"$service_ports")
    if [[ -z "$real" ]]; then
        mismatches="$mismatches $svc(no PORT= in compose)"
    elif [[ "$real" != "$port" ]]; then
        mismatches="$mismatches $svc(scrapes:$port listens:$real)"
    fi
done <<<"$prom_targets"

expect "every scrape target names the port its service listens on" "" "$mismatches"

# --- the gateway must not be scraped on its HOST port ------------------------
# `6882:80` publishes 80 as 6882 on the host. Prometheus is on the container network, where only
# 80 exists. Targeting 6882 there can never connect — and nginx serves /stub_status, not /metrics,
# which nginx-exporter already scrapes and re-exports on 9113.
expect "no scrape target uses the gateway's published host port" "0" \
    "$(grep -c "secuura-nginx-gateway:6882" <<<"$prom_live")"

# --- the stack env example must not suggest the gateway's HOST port either (KS-1388) ---
# observability/.env.example offers SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI as a commented override. The exporter runs on
# the container network, as Prometheus does, so the rule above holds for it too: 80, never the 6882 host
# publish. observability/docker-compose.yml already defaults to :80; the example must agree with it.
expect "observability/.env.example suggests the gateway's in-network status port" \
    "# SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI=http://secuura-nginx-gateway:80/stub_status" \
    "$(grep -m1 'SECUURA_NGINX_STATUS_URI=' "$DEV_ROOT/../../observability/.env.example")"

echo "prometheus_targets: ${PASS} passed, ${FAIL} failed"
(( FAIL == 0 ))
